seen_animation: A line-drawn lobster body hangs from the top centre of the frame, with a belt line across it and a V-shaped pincer on the left resting near a grey table edge; a small grey lobster sits at the left as scenery. In a.png frames 1-2 the right arm reaches down to the right edge with a narrow pincer at the bottom right corner. In frames 3-4 that arm swings inward and the pincer turns to point left, lying low near the table line. From frame 5 on, the right claw is redrawn as a wide flat shape lying horizontally across the front of the body, with several parallel lines crossing through the body outline and the left pincer, and it holds that pose almost unchanged through frame 16.
seen_film: A large dark lobster faces the camera on a cloth-covered table, with a small lobster at the left. In d.png frames 1-2 its right claw (screen right) is mostly off the right edge. In frames 3-4 the claw swings down into the lower right of the frame and curls inward. In frame 5 the claw is lifted and turned flat, and in frames 6-8 it lies horizontally across the front of the body, the big crusher claw extending to the right with its fingers pointing left over the antennae. From frame 8 to 16 the lobster holds that pose with only small settling movements.
named_subject: A lobster (the large lobster in the foreground) swinging its right claw in from the right edge and folding it horizontally across the front of its body.
evidence: Timing and placement follow the film: e.png 1-7 the right pincer hangs at the right edge as film f.png 1-7 shows the claw at the right edge; e.png 8-11 the pincer drops low and turns inward as f.png 8-11 the claw swings down and curls; e.png 17-50 holds as f.png 17-50 holds. The break is e.png 11 to 13: in 11 and 12 the claw is the doodle's thin V pincer lying low and pointing left, and in 13 it is suddenly replaced by a wide horizontal plate with long parallel lines, about twice the size, sitting higher and crossing the body; the film's f.png 11-13 shows a continuous lift-and-rotate of one claw. e.png 13 to 14 the plate shifts again (lines rearranged, outline moves left). From e.png 14 to 50 the horizontal claw is drawn as two overlapping parallel outlines with lines passing through the body and the left pincer, which reads as a doubled, transparent drawing rather than one claw in front of the body. e.png 1-6 the right arm barely moves while the film's claw shifts slightly at the edge; this is minor.
primary_gap: At e.png 12-13 the right claw pops from the doodle's thin V pincer into a different, larger, multi-line horizontal shape instead of rotating up into place as one drawing, and that replacement shape then holds for the rest of the shot.
closes_when: The same V-pincer drawing seen in e.png 9-11 visibly lifts and rotates over e.png 11-16 into the horizontal position, keeping its size and two-finger construction, and in the held pose it is drawn as one closed pincer outline lying in front of the body with no lines crossing through the body or the left pincer.
protect: The body column with its belt line and the left V pincer copied from c.png; the stable placement of the body and table line across all frames; the timing of the claw entering from the right edge (1-7), dropping and turning (8-11), and holding (17-50) in step with the film; the grey small lobster kept as scenery.
identity_gap: The body and left pincer match the doodle's construction, but from e.png 13 onward the right claw is a wide plate of parallel lines that does not use the doodle's two-stroke V pincer and overlaps the body as if transparent, so half the character no longer reads as the c.png drawing.
